new_scholarship.name: Richmond Scholars Program and Presidential Scholarships

new_scholarship.deadline: The Office of Admission publishes the Richmond Scholars deadline as "Dec 01" and states "All first-year applicants who apply by this date are automatically considered." The Scholarships for First-Year Students table states the Richmond Scholars deadline as "Submit admission application by December 1st" and the Presidential Scholarship deadline as "Submit admission application by January 1st", with the note that for Presidential Scholarships "All admission applicants are considered" and "no separate merit scholarship application is required."
new_scholarship.application_period: For the 2027 entry cycle, applications open in early August 2026. Early Decision I and Early Action applications are due November 1, 2026; the Richmond Scholars consideration deadline is December 1, 2026 and applies regardless of application plan; Early Decision II and Regular Decision applications are due January 1, 2027. Credential deadlines are November 15 (ED I), December 1 (EA), January 15 (ED II) and February 15 (RD).
application_method: This is NOT a separate scholarship application. The University states "your first-year admission application serves as your merit scholarship application, too", and for both awards "no separate application is required"; all first-year, degree-seeking applicants are automatically considered.

Submit ONE application for first-year undergraduate admission through either the Common Application or the Coalition Application, and indicate citizenship status on it. There is no separate international application.

Choose an application plan: Early Decision I, Early Action, Early Decision II or Regular Decision. IMPORTANT: to be considered for Richmond Scholars the complete application must be on file by December 1 regardless of plan, so an applicant who wants Richmond Scholars consideration must submit before December 1 even if applying Early Decision II or Regular Decision.

Complete the Richmond Question: one required essay response chosen from three published prompts, minimum 350 and maximum 650 words, submitted inside the application platform or in the Spider Portal before the credential deadline.

Have a school official send the official high school transcript (grades 9-11) and the secondary school report, and submit one recommendation letter from a school official, through the Common App/Coalition App, a third-party service (Naviance, Parchment, Scoir), email or mail.

Indicate on the application whether standardized test scores are to be considered; Richmond is test-optional for the class entering in Fall 2027. Where scores are used they must be on file by the credential deadline, and the University superscores the SAT and ACT.

Applicants whose first language is not English must arrange an official score report from TOEFL (code 5569), IELTS or the Duolingo English Test, unless an approved waiver applies. InitialView and Vericant interviews are optional supplements only.

Non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents must complete the University of Richmond Certification of Financial Responsibility in the Spider Portal (required of all international applicants, whether or not aid is sought), and the CSS Profile to the College Board (code 5569) if need-based aid is wanted, by the financial aid deadline of the chosen plan.
Submit senior progress grades as soon as they become available, and the optional arts portfolio by December 1 if arts merit scholarship consideration is wanted.

No scholarship form, nomination, interview request or portal submission is needed. Richmond Scholars finalists are notified in the Spider Portal by February 1, interviewed by a faculty selection committee over Zoom in mid-February, and final selection is completed by March 1; applicants who do not advance are not notified.
new_scholarship.description: The University of Richmond awards two prestigious merit scholarships to incoming first-year undergraduates. The Richmond Scholars Program, described by the University as its most prestigious and competitive scholarship, is given to 25 incoming students and is equal to full tuition plus housing and food, with priority course registration, guaranteed on-campus housing and eligibility for a one-time enrichment grant of up to $5,500. Presidential Scholarships, described as the University's other prestigious academic scholarship, are equal to one-third tuition and are awarded to only 10% of incoming students. Both awards are renewable for up to eight consecutive semesters of full-time enrollment and are considered automatically from the undergraduate admission application, with no separate scholarship application. Non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents receive full consideration for both, although admission review for international applicants is need-aware.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Outstanding final-year high school students of any nationality, including non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents, with a strong record in a highly rigorous curriculum plus engaged leadership, a strong sense of purpose and a commitment to a diverse and inclusive community, who can get a complete Common App or Coalition App application on file by December 1, 2026. The Richmond Scholars Program is the strongest fit for applicants who need their direct institutional costs covered in full; the Presidential Scholarship suits applicants who want recognised merit funding but can fund the remainder themselves or through need-based aid.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to all first-year, degree-seeking undergraduate applicants regardless of nationality, including non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents, who apply through the Common Application or the Coalition Application under any of the four application plans (Early Decision I, Early Action, Early Decision II, Regular Decision). International applicants are defined as students without U.S. citizenship or permanent resident status, regardless of country of residence, and are treated as international applicants even if they live in the U.S. For the Richmond Scholars Program the complete admission application must be on file by December 1 of the senior year; all first-year applicants are considered for Presidential Scholarships. Selection is holistic and highly personalised, with no GPA, percentage or class-rank threshold published; standardized tests are optional for the 2027 entry cycle. Applicants whose first language is not English must submit an official TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo English Test score or qualify for an approved waiver. Transfer students are not eligible for these first-year merit scholarships. Non-U.S. applicants are admitted need-aware and must submit the Certification of Financial Responsibility, and the CSS Profile if they want need-based aid.

new_scholarship.english_requirement: Required for applicants whose first language is not English, and NOT waived by the test-optional policy, which covers the SAT and ACT only. The University accepts official score reports for TOEFL iBT or TOEFL iBT Home Edition (institution code 5569) at 100, or 5.5 under the updated scoring scale; IELTS or IELTS Indicator at 7.5 (send to University of Richmond Undergraduate Admission, 142 UR Drive, Richmond, VA 23173); and the Duolingo English Test at 135. Waivers are available for an ACT English score of 28, an SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing score of 660, at least four years of enrollment in an academically rigorous English-medium secondary school, or an A or B equivalent grade (IB 5-7) in an AP, IB or A-level English course. Cambridge English and PTE are not listed as accepted tests. Official score reports must be sent by the testing agency - applicants cannot submit their own - although the University will accept an official report submitted by the applicant's high school if sending it is financially burdensome.
new_scholarship.selection_notes: There is no separate scholarship selection process: every first-year, degree-seeking applicant is automatically considered for merit scholarships through the admission application. The University states the evaluation is 'highly personalized and holistic' and that 'All submitted admission materials are considered in our holistic review process.' No weighting, rubric or scoring scheme is published. For the Richmond Scholars Program, applicants who advance to the finalist round are notified in the Spider Portal by February 1 (those who do not advance are not notified), finalists interview with a faculty selection committee via Zoom in mid-February, and final selection is completed by March 1. The four published Richmond Scholars criteria are academic achievement, engaged leadership, strong sense of purpose, and interest in a diverse and inclusive community; for Presidential Scholarships the University cites outstanding high school records in highly rigorous curriculums plus leadership experiences, extracurricular success and community engagement. Admission notification dates are approximately December 15 (ED I), January 25 (EA), February 15 (ED II) and April 1 (RD).
new_scholarship.notes: No substitution was required - the assigned target is not on the do-not-duplicate list in RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md and is hosted in an allowed region (United States). This record deliberately covers TWO awards published together on the same official pages, the Richmond Scholars Program (full tuition, housing and food; 25 incoming students) and Presidential Scholarships (one-third tuition; 10% of incoming students); they share the same application mechanism, the same December 1 consideration date for the higher award, and the same renewal rule, so the distinction is spelled out in coverage, benefits, tuition_coverage_note and funding_label rather than merging them into one misleading figure. No dollar amount is published for either award, because the University states their value as a share of tuition/housing/food rather than a dollar figure, so funding_amount, funding_currency and funding_period are null. The only published dollar amount connected to the award is the one-time $5,500 Enrichment Grant cap, quoted in coverage and benefits. Reference figures that ARE published and are used only as context for the cost of attending: 2026-27 tuition $70,725, housing $8,705, food $10,110, total direct costs $89,540, indirect costs $2,780 (books and supplies $1,000, personal expenses $1,710, direct loan fees $70), total cost of attendance $92,320 ($79,985 living with parents). ASSUMPTION ON THE YEAR: the admission pages publish 'December 1' and 'January 1' without calendar years. This record assigns them to the 2027 entry cycle (1 December 2026 and 1 January 2027), which is supported by the officially dated financial aid deadlines published on the same domain - November 15, 2026 for Early Action and Early Decision I and February 1, 2027 for Early Decision II and Regular Decision - by the page published as '2027 First-Year Application Materials', and by essay prompts described as appearing 'on the 2026-27 application'. ENGLISH TESTS: only TOEFL (iBT and iBT Home Edition), IELTS (and IELTS Indicator) and the Duolingo English Test are officially accepted; Cambridge English and PTE are not listed, so no Cambridge or PTE score is recorded and the published scores are described by the University as 'competitive' rather than minimum admission scores. LOGO: no University of Richmond logo file is served from a richmond.edu URL - the Brand Center serves the shield and wordmarks only from a third-party CDN and states that logos and seals are not available for download and are managed by University Communications on request - so logo_override is null and image_url is null. CONTEXT NOT PART OF THIS AWARD: the Oliver Hill Scholars award (combined 50% tuition inclusive of the Presidential Scholarship, plus up to $5,500 one-time enrichment grant, ten scholars) is noted because Oliver Hill candidates are drawn from Presidential Scholars and Richmond Scholars, but it is not one of the two awards named here. The University's average financial aid award (need-based, merit and other) to international students in 2025-26 was $69,900; that is an average across aid types, not an award amount for these merit scholarships. No official programme guide or rulebook PDF for these awards was found; the print piece at https://admission.richmond.edu/forms/pdf/print-pieces/merit-aid.pdf returns HTTP 200 with content type application/pdf but could not be rendered by the fetch tool, so no figure from it is used.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: 2027 entry; applications open August 2026, Early Decision I and Early Action due November 1 2026, Richmond Scholars consideration due December 1 2026, Early Decision II and Regular Decision due January 1 2027
programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: December 1 (1 December 2026 for the 2027 entry cycle) - submit a complete admission application for Richmond Scholars consideration
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: The Richmond Scholars consideration deadline is December 1 and applies to ALL applicants regardless of which application plan they choose: the Office of Admission states 'All first-year applicants who apply by this date are automatically considered', and the First-Year Application Materials page states 'All applications on file by December 1 (regardless of application plan) will be considered for Richmond Scholars.' An applicant who intends to apply Regular Decision or Early Decision II on January 1 must therefore submit earlier to be considered for Richmond Scholars. Presidential Scholarships have no separate deadline of their own - all first-year applicants are considered - and the merit scholarship table expresses the submission date as 'Submit admission application by January 1st', which is the Early Decision II and Regular Decision admission deadline. Two different admission-track deadline families apply to international applicants seeking need-based aid, and the earlier one (November 15, 2026 for Early Action and Early Decision I, February 1, 2027 for Early Decision II and Regular Decision) is recorded as the institutional deadline. The University publishes 'December 1' without a calendar year on the admission pages; the 2026-27 attribution used here follows the officially dated financial aid deadlines published on the same domain and the page published as '2027 First-Year Application Materials'. No cutoff time of day or timezone is published for any deadline.
programme_detail_official.status_note: The cycle is open as of 2026-10-03. Applications for the 2027 entry class are being accepted (Early Decision I and Early Action deadlines of November 1, 2026 have not yet passed at the time of verification) and the Richmond Scholars consideration deadline of December 1, 2026 is still in the future. Next expected cycle: applications open in August 2027 and the Richmond Scholars consideration deadline returns on December 1, 2027 for the 2028 entry class; the rule is published as a fixed month-and-day, so the next-cycle date should be re-verified on the official pages rather than assumed.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: Up to four years / eight consecutive semesters of full-time enrollment during the regular academic year
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: Richmond Scholars: full tuition. Presidential Scholarships: one-third of tuition only. This record covers both awards on the same official pages, so tuition_coverage is true because the Richmond Scholars Program covers tuition in full. Neither award publishes a dollar figure, so the amount is stated as a share of tuition; for reference the University's published 2026-27 tuition charge is $70,725. Neither award is guaranteed for all eight semesters - renewal depends on the terms in the initial award notification and on maintaining Satisfactory Academic Progress.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: Richmond Scholars Program: full tuition plus university housing and food for up to eight consecutive semesters, a one-time Enrichment Grant of up to $5,500, priority course registration, guaranteed on-campus housing, faculty mentorship and cohort programming. Presidential Scholarships: one-third of tuition for up to eight consecutive semesters. No stipend, travel, insurance, book or installation allowance is published for either award. No bond or service obligation is attached to either award.

programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship or residency restriction. International applicants are defined as students who are not U.S. citizens and not U.S. permanent residents, regardless of current country of residence; this includes refugees without official Form I-94 status, undocumented students and DACA students graduating from U.S. high schools. An applicant living in the United States without citizenship is still classified as international.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Explicitly open to international applicants. The Office of Financial Aid states that international students, non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents 'may receive full consideration for all merit-based scholarships, with the exception of the Army ROTC scholarship program', and that 'For full scholarship eligibility, please submit your application for admission by the December 1st Richmond Scholars deadline.' The Office of Admission states the acceptance rate for international students who do not apply for financial aid is the same as for U.S. students, while the rate for those who apply for aid is lower because Richmond is need-aware for non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents. Non-U.S. applicants must submit the Certification of Financial Responsibility, and the CSS Profile if they want need-based aid.

International applicants use the same four application plans as all other applicants and there is no separate international application. Richmond Scholars finalists are then notified in the Spider Portal by February 1 and interviewed with a faculty selection committee by Zoom in mid-February; applicants who do not advance are not notified, and final selection is completed by March 1.

Accepted tests are limited to TOEFL iBT and TOEFL iBT Home Edition, IELTS and IELTS Indicator, and the Duolingo English Test; Cambridge English and PTE are not listed as accepted. TOEFL institution code is 5569. For IELTS the University requires an exact institution address even for e-delivery: University of Richmond Undergraduate Admission, 142 UR Drive, Richmond, VA 23173. The published scores are competitive scores, not minimum admission scores: a lower-scoring applicant may still apply and will be considered, and the University 'reserves the right to require additional information to demonstrate English proficiency'. Waiver verification can take many weeks but a pending waiver does not prevent application review. InitialView and Vericant Verified Video Interviews are accepted as optional supplements and do not replace a test or waiver.

programme_detail_official.description: The University of Richmond awards two prestigious merit scholarships to incoming first-year undergraduates and considers every first-year applicant automatically, with no separate scholarship application. The Richmond Scholars Program is the University's most prestigious and competitive scholarship: it is given to 25 incoming students, is equal to full tuition plus housing and food, is renewable for up to eight consecutive semesters of full-time enrollment including study abroad, and includes priority course registration, guaranteed on-campus housing, faculty mentors, cohort programming and eligibility for a one-time enrichment grant of up to $5,500. Presidential Scholarships are the University's other prestigious academic scholarship, equal to one-third tuition, awarded to only 10% of incoming students and renewable for up to eight consecutive semesters. Richmond Scholars consideration requires a complete admission application on file by December 1 regardless of application plan, while all first-year applicants are considered for Presidential Scholarships. Non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents receive full consideration for both awards, subject to need-aware admission review, and are required to submit the University of Richmond Certification of Financial Responsibility plus the CSS Profile if they want need-based aid.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Richmond Scholars: full tuition (2026-27 published tuition $70,725), university housing ($8,705) and food ($10,110) for up to eight consecutive semesters - the University's published total direct costs for 2026-27 are $89,540 - plus priority course registration, guaranteed on-campus housing, a one-time Enrichment Grant of up to $5,500, faculty mentors, Modlin Center for the Arts ticket vouchers, cohort programming and Office of Scholars and Fellowships advising. Presidential Scholarships: one-third of tuition only, for up to eight consecutive semesters. Neither award publishes a stipend, travel, insurance, book or installation allowance, and neither covers indirect costs (2026-27: $1,000 books and supplies, $1,710 personal expenses, $70 direct loan fees where applicable; total cost of attendance $92,320) or summer study. No bond or service obligation attaches to either award.

application_readiness_checklist: Work to December 1, 2026, not to the January 1 admission deadline, if you want Richmond Scholars consideration - the cutoff applies whatever plan you choose
Open the Common App or Coalition App in early August and get the University of Richmond added
Draft the Richmond Question early: pick one of the three published prompts and write 350-650 words that answers that specific question
Brief your school counselor in September so the transcript (grades 9-11), the secondary school report and your recommendation letter land before your credential deadline

Book TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo early if English is not your first language, and order the official score report directly (TOEFL code 5569; IELTS to University of Richmond Undergraduate Admission, 142 UR Drive, Richmond, VA 23173)

Check whether you qualify for an English proficiency waiver instead: ACT English 28, SAT EBRW 660, four years in a rigorous English-medium secondary school, or an A/B equivalent (IB 5-7) in AP, IB or A-level English

If you need need-based aid, complete the Certification of Financial Responsibility and the CSS Profile (code 5569) with your admission application, not after an offer - November 15, 2026 for Early Action and Early Decision I
International applicants: use the published application fee waiver for students living abroad
Arts applicants: prepare and upload the arts portfolio by December 1 if you want it considered for merit scholarships
Add senior progress grades as soon as your school issues them; a missing grade report will not block review but must be on file before a decision is released
Watch the Spider Portal weekly after applying - finalist notification for Richmond Scholars appears there by February 1 and only finalists are contacted
If shortlisted, reserve mid-February for the Zoom interview with the faculty selection committee; final selection is completed by March 1
common_rejection_risks: Applying Regular Decision on January 1 and losing Richmond Scholars consideration entirely, because the December 1 cutoff applies regardless of plan
Assuming there is a separate scholarship form to complete, so the admission application is submitted late or incomplete

Missing the earlier financial aid deadlines (November 15, 2026 for Early Action and Early Decision I) while focusing on the December 1 merit deadline; aid filed more than 60 days late loses need-based grant eligibility altogether

As an international applicant, skipping the Certification of Financial Responsibility because you are not seeking aid - it is required of all non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents before a decision can be rendered
Assuming Richmond's test-optional policy also waives English proficiency testing; it applies only to the SAT and ACT
Assuming a Cambridge English qualification satisfies the English requirement when only TOEFL, IELTS and Duolingo are accepted
Emailing English test scores yourself instead of having the testing agency send an official report
Submitting an arts portfolio after December 1 and expecting it to be weighed for merit scholarships
Writing a generic personal statement as the Richmond Question instead of answering one of the three published prompts within 350-650 words
Falling below full-time enrollment or failing Satisfactory Academic Progress, which ends renewal even though the award is nominally renewable for eight semesters

Assuming aid will be available later if you do not receive it in your first year - the University states international students who do not receive aid in their first year are generally not assisted in following years unless funds permit

alerts.message: Richmond Scholars consideration requires a complete admission application on file by December 1, 2026, regardless of whether you choose Early Decision I, Early Action, Early Decision II or Regular Decision. Applying on January 1 forfeits Richmond Scholars.

Need-based aid deadlines are earlier than the merit deadline for early plans: November 15, 2026 for Early Action and Early Decision I, February 1, 2027 for Early Decision II and Regular Decision. Files more than 60 days late are no longer eligible for Richmond need-based grants, and files up to 60 days late lose 10% of need-based grant eligibility.

For non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents, Richmond considers ability to pay during admission review, so international applicants who apply for financial aid face a lower acceptance rate than those who do not and than U.S. applicants.

Applicants who do not advance to the Richmond Scholars finalist round are not notified, and finalist notification goes to the Spider Portal by February 1. Silence is not a rejection signal you can rely on - keep your other options open.
Richmond Scholars finalists interview with a faculty selection committee by Zoom in mid-February and final selection is completed by March 1. Block that window now if you are shortlisted.

Test-optional does not apply to English proficiency. Only TOEFL iBT/Home Edition, IELTS/IELTS Indicator and Duolingo are accepted; Cambridge English and PTE are not. Published competitive scores are TOEFL 100 (or 5.5 updated scale), IELTS 7.5 and Duolingo 135, and they are not minimum admission scores.
These merit scholarships are for incoming first-year students. Transfer students are not eligible and must instead apply for need-based financial aid.

Both awards are renewable for a maximum of eight consecutive semesters of full-time enrollment and are not available for summer study; renewal depends on the terms in your award notification and on maintaining Satisfactory Academic Progress.

research_notes.logo: No University of Richmond logo asset could be verified on the awarding body's own domain, so logo_override is null. What was tried, in order: (1) The official Brand Center primary logo set page at https://brand.richmond.edu/visual/identity/primary-logo.html was read in full. It displays the University of Richmond shield, the Richmond shield and the University/wordmark variants, but every one of those marks is served from https://d1gtq9mqg5x3oe.cloudfront.net (for example https://d1gtq9mqg5x3oe.cloudfront.net/hermes/svgs/brand/elements/identity/primary-logo/shield_ur.svg and .../wordmark_ur.svg). CloudFront is a third-party CDN host, not richmond.edu, and CDN mirrors are a hard ban. (2) The same site's Tools & Templates page was checked and states 'logos and seals are not available for download' and that they are 'managed and distributed by University Communications upon request' (brand@richmond.edu), so the University itself does not publish a downloadable logo file. (3) The homepage https://www.richmond.edu was fetched and its markup inspected: the <link rel="icon"> entries are https://d2n43swdo6jzfk.cloudfront.net/dist/img/png/favicon-32x32.png and favicon-16x16.png, and the apple-touch icons are the same CloudFront host, so the favicon route also fails the own-domain requirement. (4) No schema.org logo or official brand/press/media page on richmond.edu serves the mark itself. host_evidence therefore cannot be set to same_registrable_domain or official_brand_page, and no entry was added to official_logo_overrides.json (there is no existing richmond.edu key to dedupe against). A null logo override is an accepted honest outcome; a CloudFront-mirrored URL would be a validation failure.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: Confirmed as a bachelor's-level award from the University's own pages: the Scholarships for First-Year Students page is titled for first-year students and states 'All first-year, degree-seeking applicants, including Early Action, Early Decision I, Early Decision II, and Regular Decision applicants are eligible for merit scholarship consideration'; the Richmond Scholars page states the award is 'given to 25 incoming students' and includes 'a full-tuition, housing, and food scholarship, renewable for up to eight consecutive semesters of full-time enrollment'; the Merit-Based Aid page states these merit scholarships 'are awarded to incoming first-year students and are awarded for a maximum of four years (eight semesters) of full-time undergraduate study during the regular academic year'; and the selection page requires applicants to 'Submit a complete admission application by December 1' during their senior year. Transfer applicants are explicitly excluded, which further confirms the entry level is first-year undergraduate. The degree funded is the University of Richmond bachelor's degree (A.B. or B.S.).
research_notes.scope_note: This record covers TWO awards published together on the same official pages - the Richmond Scholars Program (full tuition, housing and food, 25 incoming students) and Presidential Scholarships (one-third tuition, 10% of incoming students). They share one application mechanism, one December 1 consideration date for the higher award and one renewal rule, so they are recorded in one object with the split made explicit in coverage, benefits, tuition_coverage_note, funding_label and estimated_uncovered_costs. Because one of the two awards is explicitly one-third tuition and neither covers indirect costs or summer study, fully_funded is false even though tuition_coverage is true for the Richmond Scholars Program; this follows the repo invariant that an uncovered component forces fully_funded false with an explanation in tuition_coverage_note. No aggregation site, listing site, Wikipedia source or aggregator such as nspscholarships.com was used - every fact comes from richmond.edu subdomains read in full.
research_notes.context_not_in_award: Noted for context but not part of this award: the Oliver Hill Scholars programme (combined 50% of tuition inclusive of the one-third-tuition Presidential Scholarship, plus up to $5,500 one-time enrichment grant, ten scholars), the Bonner Scholars Program ($3,600 annual stipend plus up to $4,500 summer support, separate application by May 8), Davis United World College Scholars (up to $30,000, need-based), Army ROTC scholarships (not open to international students), and music and theatre/dance scholarships (separate applications and auditions). The University also publishes that the average financial aid award of all types to international students in 2025-26 was $69,900; that is an average across need-based and merit aid, not an award amount for these merit scholarships.
